Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:1: This chapter will explain the teaching we copied above, "do not defile yourselves through them, lest you become defiled through them" (Leviticus 11:43), "a person defiles himself a little," and so on (Yoma 39a). It would have been fitting to explain this teaching first, since that is its order in the Talmud's discourse, but we were compelled, because of the connection of the topic we were engaged in concerning holiness - it all being one matter - and also because this teaching is mostly explained in what we explained above in the three divisions - "much," "from above," "in the World to Come," for this way applies likewise to the matter of impurity. Nevertheless, we saw fit to explain something further in it, for there is no exposition without novelty, and it is also relevant to our discourse, for by a person's knowing how to separate from impurity, he sanctifies himself through it. And so our holy Torah, in Parashat Shemini, after mentioning the impurity of foods, says (Leviticus 11:44), "and you shall sanctify yourselves," and likewise in Parashat Kedoshim concerning forbidden relations.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:2: Although it appears that the opposite of impurity is purity, as explained above under the word "purity," the Torah taught us that holiness too is the opposite of impurity. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained the reason for this in the Mechilta on the verse (Exodus 19:6), "and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" - in these words: "a holy nation" - He called them a holy nation, as it is said (2 Samuel 7:23), "and who is like Your people Israel, a nation one" - "and a holy [nation]," holy and sanctified, separated from the nations of the world - to this point. Behold, he explained the word "holiness" as the separation from the nations of the world, which is the impurity. And since this is so, we saw fit to explain everything found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that speaks of separation from impurity, relevant to this teaching, so that a person may sanctify himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:3: He said, "a person defiles himself a little, they defile him much" - according to the way explained above, it is clear that he explained "a person defiles himself" through one transgression, "they defile him much," because one transgression drags another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:4: And it is also possible to say that the intent of "they defile him much" follows the manner of what they said (Shabbat 104a), "one who comes to defile himself, they open for him" - that he has many openings through which to be defiled. And along these lines it says in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, page 169b): whoever comes to be defiled draws upon himself that impure spirit, and it cleaves to him, and how many are those who are ready to defile him, and they defile him, and he is defiled, and they defile him in this world and in that world - to this point. Behold, it says "how many are those who are ready," and so on. And the reason, as explained in Parashat Vayechi (page 228a), is that the husks are called "ready" to rest upon a person for free, and this is "they defile him much" - for each one wishes to gain possession of him and says, this one is mine.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:5: And it is also possible to explain, in saying "a person defiles himself a little," that the intent is that there are impurities not mentioned in the Torah, and it is a tradition of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that a person defiles himself through them. In the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, near the end, page 53a), Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that one who sleeps at night, a spirit of impurity rests upon his hands, and upon waking he should not touch them to his clothing or anywhere else until he washes his hands - in these words: come and see, all the people of the world, when they lie on their beds at night, and night spreads its wings over all the people of the world, they taste the taste of death, and because they taste the taste of death, that impure spirit rests upon the world and defiles the world within its bond, and rests upon his hands and he is defiled, and when he awakens and his soul returns to him, everything his hands touch is all defiled, because a spirit of impurity rests upon them - and therefore a person should not take garments to wear from one who has not washed his hands, for he has drawn upon himself that impure spirit and become defiled, and that spirit has permission to rest anywhere it finds a mark from its side. And therefore a person should not take water for washing from one who has not washed his hands, because he has drawn upon himself that impure spirit, and it is received by the one who takes water from him, and it has permission to rest upon that person. Therefore a person must guard himself on all his sides from this evil serpent, that it not rule over him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:6: And along these lines also is what he explained elsewhere, that upon waking from his sleep one should not walk four cubits before washing, and if he walked four cubits with the spirit of impurity on his hands he is like one who worships idols, and concerning this it is said (Job 12:6), "into whose hand God brings [abundance]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:7: And similar to these things to be explained are minor impurities that a person tramples with his heels, and if he defiles himself with these, they will defile him much through similar impurities, and from these he will come to grave impurities.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:8: And in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz, page 198b) he counted the matter of washing hands in the morning among the sins a person tramples with his heels, on the verse (Psalms 49:6), "why should I fear in days of evil" - and he says there that the husk has days that are called "days of evil," and concerning this David said, "why should I fear in days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels surrounds me" - in these words: what are "days of evil"? These are the days that are appointed for that evil - and what is it? This is the evil inclination, which is called "evil," and it has known days on which it is given permission in the world to defile all those whose ways are defiled, for whoever comes to be defiled, they defile him, and these are called "days of evil," and they are appointed over those sins that people tread with their heels. Come and see, all those whose ways are defiled - how many bands of destroyers are appointed against them and defile them, on the path a person wishes to walk, on that very path they lead him. If a person comes to purify himself, how many assist him! For we have learned that when a person rises in the morning he must wash his hands from a vessel of water, for it is a vessel from which to take water from one who has already washed his hands, as they established. And come and see, concerning this vessel we established the matter, and further, a person should wash his right hand with his left, in order for the right to rule over the left, and the right is washed by the left - and this is why it is called netilah [lifting] - and therefore, whoever washes his hands should wash the right with the left, to make the right rule over the left, so as not to give the evil inclination any place to rule at all, and this we have established - to this point. Behold, all these fine points of the commandment assist a person's purification, and if he tramples them with his heels, they defile him, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:9: And similarly they said in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 77a), in these words: these matters King Solomon revealed in the book of Ashmedai the king, and I found in it one thousand four hundred and fifty kinds of impurity by which people are defiled, which Ashmedai revealed to King Solomon - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:10: And among the impurities one must be careful of what they said in the Talmud (Horayot 13b): one who passes between two women, between two camels, and all those things that cause forgetting of one's learning, which we shall copy below, with God's help - all of these are minor impurities not mentioned in the Torah, which a person tramples with his heels. And among these is what they said in the Talmud (Makkot 16b), that one who holds back his needs transgresses "you shall not make yourselves detestable" (Leviticus 11:43), and likewise one who drinks from the cupping-instrument of the bloodletter - and these are minor impurities that a person tramples with his heels. And likewise several things the commentators, of blessed memory, explained that one who does them needs to wash his hands, such as one who cuts his nails, removes his shoes, touches his feet, or scratches his head, and many similar things that the honorable Maharik, may his light shine, copied in Beit Yosef (Tur, Orach Chaim, siman 4).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:11: "From below, they defile him from above" - already explained in the matter of holiness, and along that same way they defile him from above, in that when his soul ascends above every night, they keep away from him and proclaim about him that he is impure.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:12: And further, as we copied in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9, several angels curse him and say, "clear away from around so-and-so, for his testimony is on his face, and an impure spirit rests upon him" (Parashat Acharei, page 76a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:13: But there are further aspects on this found in the words of Rashbi, fitting to copy here. "From below" - it is possible to explain that its meaning is that he defiles himself with the powers of Na'amah that spread below among people, appearing to them in the likeness of beautiful women, causing them to emit seed in vain, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 55a) - see there, in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, woe to those people who do not know, do not pay attention, and do not observe, and are all closed off, not knowing how full the world is with strange creatures that are not visible, and with hidden matters - for if permission were given to the eye to see, people would be astonished how they could exist in the world. Come and see, this Na'amah, the mother of demons, was, and so on - see there. And the word "below" fits along these lines better than what was explained, because these powers are below the firmament, and all the air is full of them, as explained, and moreover they spread below among people.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:14: And Rashbi explained there, before this, that these powers cleave only to one who is of their kind, in these words: come and see, every person who goes to the left side and defiles his ways draws upon himself all impure spirits, and an impure spirit cleaves to him and does not leave him, and its cleaving, that of the impure spirit, is to this person and no other, and therefore their cleaving is only to those who cleave to them. Happy are the righteous who walk on the straight path, and they are truly righteous, and their children are righteous in the world, and concerning them it is written (Proverbs 2:21), "for the upright shall dwell in the land" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:15: And so he also said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, page 169b), that when a person walks on the straight path these powers do not encounter him, and concerning him it is said (Psalms 91:10), "no evil shall befall you" - this is Lilith - "nor shall any plague come near your tent" - and "plague" refers to human afflictions.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:16: "They defile him from above" - it is possible to explain this by what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 54a), in these words: what is "all the days of her flux, her impurity" (Leviticus 15:25)? Rather, the wicked defile themselves through their sins, for themselves. Along these lines is what is said in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 54a), that if one sinned and a spirit of impurity rested upon him, and he fathers a son before he repents, that son draws upon himself the power of impurity - in these words: come and see, at the time a person walks in the true path and draws upon himself a supernal holy spirit and it cleaves to him, the son he begets into the world - he draws upon him supernal holiness, and he shall be holy with the holiness of his Master, as it is written (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy," and so on. But when he walks on the left side and draws upon himself an impure spirit and it cleaves to him, the son he brings forth into the world - he draws upon him a spirit of impurity, and he shall be defiled with the defilement of that side, and concerning this it is written (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward," and so on - to this point, relevant here. And my teacher, peace be upon him, testified concerning a certain Jewish youth who converted to the Ishmaelite faith, and afterward converted to yet another faith, and it was testified concerning him that both those transgressions had been in his father.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:17: And let us return to our matter, for along these lines it is possible to explain "they sanctify him from above," meaning in order that he draw a holy soul for his son - and this is included in everything explained above concerning "they sanctify him from above."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:18: Now, according to the way explained above concerning one who sanctifies himself "from below," which is the holiness of the five senses, it would have been necessary for us to elaborate here on the matter of the impurity of the senses, if he defiled them, how great is the blemish and impurity that reaches him - but because we must explain below the holiness of the five senses, each one on its own, we shall also explain, in passing, the matter of impurity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:19: "In this world, they defile him for the World to Come" - according to the way explained above concerning "this world," which is the holiness of thought, likewise concerning impurity, it is the impurity of thought in all the affairs of this world, and its punishment is severe, that they defile him for the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:20: And the reason is that the limbs act only through the participation of thought, whether toward holiness or the opposite - and concerning holiness we have already explained; and concerning impurity, there are aspects to it, for one who sins by chance is not the same as one who plots schemes for how to commit the transgression - for just as in holiness, a good thought for a commandment effects a repair above, so a thought of transgression blemishes in the world of thought, and he is exempted from there [only] in that once his thought comes into deed, he is then judged even for the thought - and with this the verses and the sayings of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, are reconciled, for they said (Kiddushin 40a), "the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join an evil thought to a deed," as it is said (Psalms 66:18), "if I had regarded iniquity in my heart, the LORD would not have heard" - yet we find that King David, peace be upon him, said elsewhere (Psalms 36:5), "he devises iniquity upon his bed, he sets himself in a way that is not good," and so on - so we see that they do reckon the evil thought, but on the condition we explained - when the evil thought comes into deed, namely "he sets himself in a way that is not good."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:21: And so they said in the Midrash (Yalkut Isaiah, remez 395) on the verse (Isaiah 3:10), "say of the righteous that it shall be well with him," and so on, in these words: a good thought - the Holy One, blessed be He, joins it to a deed, as it is said (Malachi 3:16), "then those who feared the LORD spoke," and so on - what is "and to those who thought upon His name"? Rabbi Yose said, even if one thought to perform a commandment and did not perform it, Scripture accounts it to him as though he had performed it. An evil thought - the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join it to a deed, as it is said, "if I had regarded iniquity in my heart, the LORD would not have heard" - but then what is meant by "behold, I am bringing upon this people the fruit of their thoughts" (cf. Jeremiah 6:19)? A thought that produces fruit, the Holy One, blessed be He, joins it to a deed; one that does not produce fruit, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join it to a deed. "And in order to seize the house of Israel by their heart" (Ezekiel 14:5) - this is written concerning idolatry - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:22: And along the lines we explained, it is possible that "a thought that produces fruit" is called such whether it comes into deed or does not come into deed - for example, he thought to steal and stole, or did not steal.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:23: And it is also possible to say "a thought that produces fruit" is like what they said, of blessed memory (Avodah Zarah 20b), on "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10) - that one should not have lustful thoughts by day and come to impurity at night. Behold, the thought from which an evil fruit emerged - which is the impurity of a seminal emission that begets a demon or a harmful spirit in the world, for the children a person begets are called his "fruit," as is known. And when it is a thought that did not come to impurity, it is a thought that does not produce fruit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:24: And this is when he dwelt long on that lustful thought and brought himself to dwell upon it, as they said in Tractate Niddah (13b), "whoever brings himself to dwell upon lustful thoughts is not admitted into the enclosure of the Holy One, blessed be He," as it is said (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" - for then he certainly comes to impurity and emits seed in vain, which is called "evil," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach, page 158a). But if a lustful thought came to him and he cast it from his heart, he has not produced fruit, and it is not accounted to him as the sin of lustful thought, for they said, of blessed memory (Bava Batra 164b), "there are three things from which no person is saved every day, and one of them is thoughts of transgression." And it is concerning such a lustful thought that produces fruit that they said in the teaching, that if one defiles himself in this world, they defile him for the World to Come. And how precise is the word "this world" in this explanation - for this world became corrupted through the sin of the first man, "and they knew that they were naked" (Genesis 3:7), and they came to know what nakedness is, which was not so before. It follows that if he sanctifies his thought not to think of women, they sanctify him, and likewise the opposite, as stated.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:25: And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat Kedoshim 24:6), that all holiness is holiness from forbidden relations, in these words: why was the portion of forbidden relations juxtaposed to the portion of holiness? To teach you that wherever you find a fence against forbidden relations, you find holiness, and whoever fences himself from forbidden relations is called holy. Rabbi Yehoshua of Sichnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi, he brings this from the Shunammite woman - this is what is written (2 Kings 4:9), "and she said to her husband, behold now, I know that this is a holy man of God" - he is holy but his attendant is not holy, teaching that she never looked upon him. The Rabbis say that she never saw, and so on. The maidservant of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said, I used to handle the garments of my master, and never in my days did I see anything untoward on my master's garments - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:26: And after we have found all these aspects concerning the matter of a woman's nakedness, which is called holiness, likewise the holiness of thought is called simply "holiness," which includes everything - for even if a person sees a woman, if he does not let his heart's thought stray after her, the sight has not harmed him. The proof of this is that Rabbi Yehudah bar Ila'i would dance before the bride, and she seemed to him like a beam (cf. Ketubot 17a), and likewise a certain rabbi to whom she seemed like white geese (Berachot 20a) - and all this is because their thoughts were separated from the affairs of this world and cleaved always to the blessed Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:27: And so, if he defiles his thought with matters of forbidden relations, certainly they defile him for the World to Come, for he is uprooted from there, as they elaborated in the Zohar, in the Tosefta (Parashat Vayetze, page 154b). It says there that a voice is aroused from the Shechinah every day in the Garden of Eden, calling loudly and saying: whoever among you enters and exits and takes hold of the Tree of Life, reaches its branches and grasps its roots, eats of its fruit sweet as honey, gives water to the soul, healing to the body - let him guard himself from an evil thought, from a thought that betrays the Tree of Life, that defiles the river and the stream, the source of Israel, which gives death to the soul and breaking to the body - it has no permanence at all. A thought that defiles that source of his - because that thought ascends and exchanges soul for soul, the Tree of Life withdraws and the Tree of Death takes hold of him, the soul is drawn from there - woe to him who is uprooted through that thought from the Tree of Life and cleaves to the Tree of Death; it has no branches, it never sees good, it is dry, utterly without moisture, its fruit bitter as wormwood - concerning it is said (Jeremiah 17:6), "and he shall be like a shrub in the desert, and shall not see when good comes," and so on. Because a good thought ascends above and takes hold of the Tree of Life, grasps its branches, eats of its fruits, all sanctities and all blessings emerge from it, it inherits life for its soul and healing for its body - concerning it is said (Jeremiah 17:8), "and he shall be like a tree planted by the waters, and spreads out its roots by the stream, and shall not fear when heat comes," and so on. All things of the world follow after thought and lustful reflection, and therefore, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" (Leviticus 20:7), because all the sanctities of the world are brought forth and drawn by a good thought - to this point. And the conclusion of the teaching's words: therefore in prayer one needs will and thought to direct, and so in all those services of the Holy One, blessed be He, thought and reflection perform the deed and draw the drawing-down in whatever is needed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:28: Behold, in this teaching our intent is clearly explained, both concerning the holiness of thought - that what is said, "and you shall sanctify yourselves," and so on, refers to the holiness of thought - and concerning an evil thought, that it uproots itself from the Tree of Life, which is in Atzilut. And there are two aspects to lustful thought, as he explained in the teaching: the first is a simple lustful thought that brings one to impurity, as they said, that one should not have lustful thoughts by day and come to impurity at night - and this is what he said, "let him guard himself from an evil thought, from a thought that betrays the Tree of Life, that defiles the river and the stream, the source of Israel" - and this is the blemish of the sign of the covenant, which is called the river and stream, the source of Israel, being the source of the drawing-down of the souls of Israel, and the emission of that drop, which should have brought forth a soul in holiness, went out in vain through Lilith, as explained above - and it is a great blemish to the sign of the covenant. And the second is thinking of another woman during marital relations, which is called "changeling children," as they explained, of blessed memory (Nedarim 20b, Tur Orach Chaim, siman 240).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:29: Now, from what he said, "because a good thought ascends above and takes hold of the Tree of Life," and so on, "all things of the world follow after thought and lustful reflection" - we may derive from this a third division: that every evil thought to commit a transgression causes a blemish, for just as a thought for a commandment effects a repair for the soul, as they said, that a good thought, in every detail of a commandment, ascends above and takes hold of the Tree of Life, so, conversely, it takes hold of the Tree of Death. And this is what was explained above, in the first explanation, that the author of the teaching said "a person defiles himself in this world" - the intent being the impurity of thought in all the affairs of this world, and therefore they defile him for the World to Come, because he is uprooted from holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:30: And concerning the members of this group, may the Merciful One save us from them, it is said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 25a) that they are the destroyers of the world - after speaking of the virtue of one who acquires nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, he said, of blessed memory: happy is his portion, whoever inherits this supernal inheritance; woe to those wicked ones whose souls do not merit in this world, all the more so in the World to Come - concerning them it is written (1 Samuel 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies, He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling" - for they go about and roam the world and find no place to be bound to, and are defiled within the side of impurity, and a herald calls out and says (Leviticus 5:15), "if a soul commits a trespass against the LORD" - "the sanctuary of the LORD has he defiled" - for he did not enter or become included in holiness, and they become destroyers of the world, because [impure spirits] cleave to them and they are defiled - to this point. Behold, it is explained in this teaching clearly how they defile him for the World to Come, for they are called destroyers of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:31: And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 70a) they raised a question on this, where Rabbi Yehudah said there that the souls of the wicked are the destroyers, and Rabbi Yose said, if so, it is good for the wicked to become destroyers in the world - where then is the punishment of Gehinnom, where the evil appointed for them in that world? Rabbi Chiya said, so we have learned, and so we have established the matter: the souls of the wicked, when they leave the world, several officers of judgment are appointed to receive them, to bring them into Gehinnom, and they bring them in through three judgments every day of Gehinnom; afterward they are paired with them and go about and roam the world, and they lead astray the wicked whose repentance is blocked before them, then they return them to Gehinnom and they are defiled there, and so every day; afterward, once they have gone about and roamed the world, they return to their graves, and there the worm of the body gnaws the flesh, and they mourn over it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:32: And so it is also explained at the end of the teaching we copied from Parashat Vayera (page 99a), at the end of chapter 4, where it says, just as a person is drawn from this world, so they draw him when he departs from this world - if in holiness, and so on; if in impurity, that side draws him to itself and he becomes one of them, cleaving to them, and they are called the harmers of people, and so on - and this is what they said, of blessed memory (Zohar, Parashat Acharei Mot, page 70a; cf. Parashat Mishpatim, page 118a), "the souls of the wicked are themselves the harmers." And in our days we have seen this matter several times here in Safed, upper Galilee, and there are several eyewitnesses to the matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:33: Therefore happy is he who sanctifies his soul and body in this world, so that his soul may cleave to the supernal holy ones, to behold the pleasantness of the LORD and to visit in His sanctuary. And with this the chapter is concluded.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 5:34: And after we have explained the generalities of holiness, let us come to explain the particulars of holiness fitting for each and every limb, as found in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, and in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:1: Because we preceded, in the previous chapter, our engagement with the matter of the holiness of thought, and that it is the essential thing in divine service, for a person to cleave to his Maker and draw holiness upon himself, as in the teaching of Rashbi, peace be upon him, which we copied, that all sanctities are drawn by a good thought - and along these lines is what they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 13a), "commandments require intent," and so most halachic authorities ruled - it follows that if one performed a commandment or was occupied with Torah without intent, it is as though he did nothing, and he must go back and do it [again]. And several mishnahs prove this (Berachot chapter 2, mishnah 1): one who was reading in the Torah and the time for the Shema recitation arrived - if he directed his heart, he has fulfilled his obligation. And so with his prayer, the early pious ones would tarry an hour so that they might direct their hearts to the Omnipresent (Berachot chapter 5, mishnah 1). And so, one who immersed [in a mikveh] but was not established [with intent] is as though he had not immersed (Chagigah chapter 2, mishnah 6). And further, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (cf. Berachot 34b, Tur Orach Chaim, siman 101), if he did not direct his intent in the [blessing of] the Patriarchs, he must return to the beginning, and so on. All these are settled halachot, showing that a person's repair of his thought is through intent - therefore we saw fit to explain in this chapter the way for a person to sanctify his thoughts and the reflections of his heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:2: The instruments of thought are known to be two, the brain and the heart, and upon them depend love and fear, as we copied the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Love, chapter 2, that concerning these it is said (Deuteronomy 29:28), "the hidden things belong to the LORD our God" - and as he also explained in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 123b): "the hidden things" are fear and love, which are in the brain and heart, within the cavity of the body and in the head; and "the revealed things" are the Torah and the commandments, which are in the body and head, externally. And the secret of the matter is truly so - if a person fears the Holy One, blessed be He, or loves Him, certainly no other person knows, because it is a matter not revealed except between him and his Maker; but a person occupied with Torah and walking in the positive commandments is revealed to every person, because the Holy One, blessed be He, made for him a mouth revealed, to be occupied with Torah, and eyes to look and ears to hear it, and the Holy One, blessed be He, made for a person hands and feet to perform positive commandments with them - to this point. And he explained there, before this, that fear and love are Yud-Heh, and concerning them, "the hidden things belong to YHVH our God," which are Abba and Imma; "the revealed things" are Vav-Heh, which are son and daughter, Torah and commandment, and they are revealed because they are seen by people through the revealed limbs, as explained in the teaching.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:3: And in actuality, the matter is so in the supernal Atzilut, as explained in the Introduction to the Tikkunim (page 17a), in the words of Elijah, of blessed memory - he said that the reality of the revealed limbs is: Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferet the torso, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, and Yesod the end of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchut is the mouth, called the Oral Torah; the brain is Chokhmah, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands - and concerning these two it is written, "the hidden things belong to YHVH our God" - to this point. Behold, the revealed limbs are from the six extremities downward, namely Vav-Heh, the revealed; and the brain and heart, which are hidden within the body, are Chokhmah and Binah, and they are hidden for two reasons: first, in the reality of the limbs themselves, being within the cavity of the body; and second, because the brain is a vessel in which thought rests, and thought is spiritual and hidden, and the heart is a vessel in which understanding rests, for a person to understand and know, which is likewise a hidden action - and this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise about in saying, "the brain is Chokhmah, it is thought within," and likewise "Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands," to indicate the two aspects mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:4: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 247b), it is explained that the three brains in a person - meaning the three powers in the brain - correspond to the three yuds in the Name Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled out with alefs [Yud-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Alef, Vav-Alef-Vav, Heh-Alef], in these words: further, "mixed with beaten oil" (Numbers 28:5) - this is the Righteous One [Yesod], living forever, who draws holy drops that trickle like olives from the supernal brain, which are one-tenth corresponding to the Yud, and two-tenths, and three-tenths - and these are a tenth for a lamb, and two-tenths for a ram, and three-tenths for a bull. And the secret of the matter, they said in [the tractate on] fasts (page 25b), no drop descends without two drops ascending to correspond to it - and these are, in secret and by allusion, corresponding to the three brains: one, the brain of memory; the second, the brain of thought; the third, the brain of imagination. Imagination and memory ascend from the heart, thoughts descend upon them to the heart and receive them as a king, because this is the thought that rides and rules over the third living creature, and two living creatures descend to it, and open their wings to receive it, like a cholam over a tzeirei forming a segol - and this is the supernal crown over Chokhmah and Binah - to this point. And so too in the Tikkunim (page 126a) they explained the three brains corresponding to the three yuds of the Name mentioned - see there. And we must say that these three brains are in Ze'ir Anpin, for in Arich [Anpin] there is one hidden brain, as explained in the Idra.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:5: And once a person knows that his whole body and its limbs were built according to the order of the supernal Atzilut, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 130b), whose wording we copied in the Gate of Fear (chapter 9), and knows that his thought corresponds to the supernal thought, he should intend that the limbs of his brain and heart, which are his most excellent limbs, upon which life depends, be prepared to direct and think holy thoughts, and purify his thoughts properly - for if he thinks in his brain and heart thoughts that are not fitting, the power of Chokhmah and Binah depart from him. And the reason is that just as the revealed limbs are blemished through the act of physical transgression, so these primary hidden limbs are blemished through an impure thought, and since it is blemished, the supernal King does not cause His spiritual power of Chokhmah and Binah to rest there - and so it is proven in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz, page 196a) concerning Joseph the righteous, peace be upon him, that he was rewarded for every single limb that he did not blemish, and they said concerning the matter of thought, in these words: a thought that he did not think is called understanding and wise - to this point. Therefore the repair of the brain and heart is to think holy thoughts, and through this he causes the Name Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs to rest in the thought of his brain and heart, and he should direct his intent to the source of holiness, which is the fully-spelled four-letter Name with yuds, which totals seventy-two [in gematria], and through this he sanctifies his thoughts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:6: And with this the wording of Rashbi, peace be upon him, which we copied in the previous chapter, is precise, where he said, "and therefore, 'and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy,' because all the sanctities of the world are brought forth and drawn by a good thought." And you already know what we explained above, in chapter 2, that Chokhmah is the source of holiness in the secret of the Name mentioned, for there is no holiness less than ten - and happy is he who directs his intent to this while occupied with Torah, to draw the kindness of the Name mentioned upon his thought, for he certainly sanctifies himself, since the Torah draws holiness, as explained in Parashat Kedoshim, that the Torah is drawn from Chokhmah, and by directing his intent to the source of holiness he certainly draws holiness - in these words (Zohar, page 81a): we have learned, the holiness of Torah is a holiness that ascends above all holinesses, and the holiness of the supernal Chokhmah ascends above all - he said to him, there is no Torah without Chokhmah, and no Chokhmah without Torah, and so on - to this point, relevant here.
